outcomes: A user reads the version every version line is at with putnami version get, and releases one line with putnami version tag, which writes its changelog, its release commit and its tag
A user prepares the release notes of several lines with putnami version notes, which writes every line's changelog in one commit to review before any tag
A release is reviewable before it happens: version tag prints the proposed tag and its changelog and writes nothing without --yes
The versions come from the putnami process that launched the command, so version get prints and version tag releases what the core computes from git
nonGoals: Computing a version: the core computes every version, proposed release and line history, and answers them through version.lines
Running from a hosted run or from a putnami process that opens no host channel
Knowing the layout of a workspace: version notes names the other files the last release modified and writes none of them

text: putnami version get prints one row per version line: two spaces, the line's scope path, or (workspace root) for the root line, a space and the version the host answers. --scope names one line, with or without its slashes.
Under --output=json or jsonl it prints one result envelope for version get, whose data is the line's record, or an array of records when there are several.

requirements.text: When the host answers from a recorded dependency graph because it could not refresh the graph a support catalog reads, version get says so on standard error and prints that answer, and version tag refuses with exit status 1.

putnami version tag --yes renders the line's changelog from the commits the host lists, writes it into the line's CHANGELOG.md, commits it as chore(release): <line> <version> with the human's Co-Authored-By trailer, then creates the annotated tag on that commit with the changelog as its message. --push then pushes HEAD and the tag to origin.

text: The rendered changelog carries no tracker reference: #<number>, <owner>/<repository>#<number> and the word before them, such as issue, leave each commit subject, with the brackets that hold nothing else. After such a word the # is optional.

When CHANGELOG.md opens with a level-one heading, the release goes under that title and its introduction. A missing or empty file is created with the title # Changelog — <line>, or # Changelog for the root line.
Without --yes, version tag writes nothing: --dry-run prints the line, the version and the tag it proposes, then the changelog, and otherwise it prints the release and asks for --yes.
An explicit tag replaces the proposed one when it is the line's tag pattern with a MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version.

version tag exits 2 and writes nothing when the workspace declares several lines and --scope names none, HEAD carries the line's release tag, an explicit tag is not a release tag of the line, the host is bound to a commit other than HEAD, the tree is dirty, the tag exists, the host proposes no release and no tag is named, or the output mode is json or jsonl.
It exits 1, not 2, for a dependency graph the host could not refresh and for a failure of git.

putnami version notes <line>@<version>... --yes writes the notes of each named line into its CHANGELOG.md as version tag renders them, at the named version, and makes one commit on the current branch that names every line and version with the human's Co-Authored-By trailer. / names the root line. It tags and pushes nothing.
It then names the other files of the workspace that the last release commits of the lines modified, and writes none.

requirements.text: Without --yes, version notes writes nothing: --dry-run prints, for each named line in order, the changelog file, the line, the version and the notes, then the files it names, and otherwise it prints the lines and versions and asks for --yes.

text: version notes exits 2 and writes nothing for no line, a line named twice or unknown, a version that is not MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH or not above the line's last release, an existing tag, a tagged HEAD, a version its CHANGELOG.md already holds, a host bound to another commit, and the output mode json or jsonl. Without --dry-run, it also exits 2 and writes nothing for a dirty tree, the default branch and a detached HEAD.
It exits 1 for a dependency graph the host could not refresh and for a failure of git.
An unexpected argument or --scope without a value exits 2 with the reason on standard error.
A scope that names no line and an invalid configuration the host refuses exit 2, and a failure of the host exits 1, each with the host's message.
Without a host channel the commands exit 1 and name the interactive launch that opens one.

The manifest declares the version command group, whose default is get, with interactive get, notes and tag subcommands that run the executable in the workspace root without a cache. notes and tag declare the dry-run flag the core forwards.
The executable runs version get, version notes and version tag with the job context argument putnami appends removed.
